title: The Score of Students Solving Math Expression
summary: Given a string s containing digits and the operators '+' and '*', representing a valid math expression of single-digit numbers, compute the correct answer by first performing all multiplications from left to right, followed by all additions from left to right.
statement: Given a string s containing digits and the operators '+' and '*', representing a valid math expression of single-digit numbers, compute the correct answer by first performing all multiplications from left to right, followed by all additions from left to right. An integer array answers is provided, containing the answers submitted by students. Grade each answer as follows: - Award 5 points if the answer matches the correct result. - Award 2 points if the answer could be the result of incorrectly applying the operators but still has correct arithmetic. - Award 0 points otherwise. Return the total points awarded to the students.
constraints: s alternates single digits with + or * and has at most 31 characters; answers has at most 10000 entries.
Award five for the standard-precedence result, two for a result from some parenthesization with correct arithmetic, otherwise zero.
Only plausible intermediate results at most 1000 are retained.
hints: Correct grading needs both standard precedence and every result obtainable by changing only parenthesization.
Compute the correct total with multiplication runs; use interval DP sets for all binary splits.
possible(l,r) unions a op b for every cut and cached subinterval result; score answers by correct first, then membership.
Every full parenthesization has a unique final split, so interval DP enumerates all and only arithmetic-order mistakes; separate precedence evaluation identifies five-point answers.
